findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, disabling passkeys on normal login
findings.body: The new helper returns true only when `user != null`. Before this change, passkeys were set up only when the user was not yet identified. In `authenticate()` and `challenge()` the call is now `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`. On a fresh login the user is null, so `fillContextForm` is never called and the conditional passkey UI is gone. That breaks the main passkeys login path, which several existing tests expect to show the webauth form before the username is entered. The condition looks inverted, or the null check should simply be removed.

findings.title: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no argument
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only method defined, in `UsernamePasswordForm`, takes a `UserModel` parameter, so this code will not compile. It should pass `context.getUser()`, or a no-argument overload should be added.
